clue.text: One royal lady among many appearing in the newspapers

definitions.text: One royal lady among many appearing in the newspapers

parts.words: One royal lady among many appearing in the newspapers
parts.note: read as a description of a king's daughter, one of the many royal women whose doings fill the press

explanation.surface: Yet another royal woman makes the papers.
explanation.definitionFit: A king's or queen's daughter is a royal lady, and such women were a staple of the tabloid press.

clue.text: Chicken not fully occupied?

explanation.surface: A timid bird, or a coward with nothing to do.
explanation.walkthrough: Partlet is an old name for a hen (Chaucer's Pertelote); read as two words, part let, it describes a building only partly rented out.
explanation.definitionFit: Partlet is a traditional name for a hen, and a house partly rented to tenants is only partly occupied.

clue.text: Sandwich material

explanation.walkthrough: To interline is to insert between lines; as a noun it is the padding layer sewn between a garment's lining and outer cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: To write between lines of text is to sandwich words in, and the hidden padding layer of a coat is sandwiched fabric.

clue.text: Involving rich doctors returning a baptismal robe

indicators.note: to involve is literally to roll up or entangle, so the word rich is twisted into a new order
returning tells us the word for doctors is read backwards

parts.note: MOS, medical officers, the military name for doctors

explanation.surface: A christening gown made with the help of wealthy physicians.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Involving' scrambles RICH to CHRI; 'returning' turns MOS (medical officers) into SOM.
explanation.definitionFit: A chrisom is the white cloth or gown put on a child at baptism.

clue.text: Resolute enough to put a stop to the blood-shed

definitions.text: to put a stop to the blood-shed

explanation.surface: Firm enough to halt the bleeding.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is the verb, a variant of stanch, to stop the flow of blood; the hyphen in blood-shed hints at shed blood.
explanation.definitionFit: A staunch supporter is steadfast and loyal, and to staunch a wound is to stem its bleeding.

clue.text: A politician must be in step, that's plain

indicators.note: must be in places the article and the politician within the dance step

parts.note: a pas is a step in ballet
MP, Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: An MP has to keep in line, which is obvious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plain' looks like the adjective 'obvious'; it is the noun, a flat grassland.
explanation.definitionFit: The pampas are the vast treeless grasslands of South America.

clue.text: Stay with a football crowd to increase the strain

parts.note: a stay is a support, a prop
the gate is the attendance at a match

explanation.surface: Being stuck with the crowd at a match only adds to the stress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strain' looks like stress; it is a breed or line, which you increase by breeding.
explanation.definitionFit: To propagate plants or animals is to breed them, multiplying a variety or line.

clue.text: Communist teams offered in place of trade

indicators.note: offered in means set inside the marketplace

parts.note: a mart is a market
an XI is a team of eleven, as in cricket or football, so teams are XIS

explanation.surface: Red sides put up for sale at the market.
explanation.definitionFit: A follower of Karl Marx's doctrine is a communist.

clue.text: Performer in a difficult part is terribly nervous

indicators.note: in signals that the answer sits inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: An actor given a tough role suffers dreadful stage fright.
explanation.walkthrough: The run 'part is terribly' holds the answer across its words; 'a difficult' and 'nervous' complete the picture only.
explanation.definitionFit: An artiste is a professional entertainer such as a singer or dancer.

clue.text: The sailor delivered round and round, getting slower

indicators.note: round means the word for delivered is wrapped about the sailor

parts.note: rid means delivered or freed
TAR, a sailor
taken as written
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: The seaman made his rounds, steadily losing pace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'delivered' looks like handed over, but here it means freed (rid of); 'round' is used twice, once as a wrapper and once as the letter O.
explanation.definitionFit: Ritardando is the musical direction to slow down gradually.

clue.text: Estimate speed

explanation.definitionFit: To rate is to assess or value something, and a rate is a pace such as miles per hour.

clue.text: The flower of the aristocracy

explanation.definitionFit: This is the cuckoo pint or wild arum, a hedgerow plant, and also a phrase for peers and peeresses collectively.

clue.text: "Hail to the Chief who in advances!" (Scott)

definitions.text: "Hail to the Chief who in advances!" (Scott)

parts.words: "Hail to the Chief who in advances!" (Scott)
parts.note: a line from Walter Scott's The Lady of the Lake with its key noun left out for the solver to supply

explanation.walkthrough: The full line is a boat song in Scott's poem The Lady of the Lake; the missing word means victory.
explanation.definitionFit: The quotation is completed by a word for a great victory or celebration of success.

clue.text: Pole joining an establishment maybe

parts.note: a perch is an old measure of length, also called a rod or pole
taken as written
CE, the Church of England, the established church

explanation.surface: A Pole joins the firm, possibly.
explanation.walkthrough: The Established Church in England is the Church of England, CE.
explanation.definitionFit: Perchance is an old-fashioned word for perhaps.

clue.text: A big cat — all the Russian leader wanted

parts.note: pan- is a prefix meaning all
taken as written

indicators.note: the first letter of the word it picks from

parts.note: the first letter of Russian

explanation.surface: A large feline was everything the Tsar desired.
explanation.definitionFit: A panther is a leopard, especially a black one, one of the large wild felines.

clue.text: He has a simple answer for every complaint

definitions.text: He has a simple answer for every complaint

parts.words: He has a simple answer for every complaint
parts.note: a simple is an old word for a medicinal plant, so this healer has a plant remedy for each ailment

explanation.definitionFit: Such a practitioner treats illness with plant remedies, once called simples.

clue.text: Soldiers in very quiet surroundings are to get ready

indicators.note: in sets the soldiers within the very quiet surroundings

parts.note: pp, pianissimo, is very quiet in music
RE, the Royal Engineers
taken as written

explanation.surface: Troops in near silence are to make ready.
explanation.definitionFit: To prepare is to make ready for something.

clue.text: Not to indulge is such a burden!

explanation.surface: Abstinence is such a chore!
explanation.walkthrough: 'burden' looks like a load; it is the old word for a song's chorus.
explanation.definitionFit: To refrain is to abstain, and a refrain is the repeated chorus of a song, also called its burden.

clue.text: Penny tried a new make-up for a part in "The Winter's Tale"

parts.note: P, penny

indicators.note: new make-up means the letters of tried a are rearranged

explanation.surface: Penny experimented with fresh cosmetics for a Shakespeare role.
explanation.definitionFit: Perdita is the lost daughter of Leontes in Shakespeare's play.

clue.text: Always to be in the right, that is the dream

indicators.note: to be in places the word for always inside the other pieces

parts.note: R, right
IE, id est, that is
ever means always

explanation.surface: Never being wrong is the ideal.
explanation.definitionFit: A reverie is a daydream.

clue.text: Early-morning caller given a roll with nothing in it

indicators.note: in it means the round letter goes inside the list of names

parts.note: a roster is a roll or list of names
O, zero

explanation.surface: The dawn visitor is handed an empty bread roll.
explanation.walkthrough: 'roll' looks like bread; it is a list. 'caller' is the bird that crows at dawn.
explanation.definitionFit: The cock crows at dawn, waking everyone.

clue.text: Peter loses his head in front of the old serving man

indicators.note: in places the beheaded name inside the word for the front

parts.note: the van is the front, as in vanguard

indicators.note: loses his head means the name drops its first letter

explanation.surface: Peter is beheaded before the elderly servant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loses his head' leaves ETER, which goes 'in' VAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A veteran is an old soldier, one who has served long.

clue.text: An adaptation of mice, not of insects

indicators.note: an adaptation of the words reworks their letters into a new form

explanation.surface: A version of mice, which are not bugs.
explanation.definitionFit: Entomic means relating to insects, as in entomology.

clue.text: Stop threat from being made generally

indicators.note: being made means the letters are put together afresh

explanation.surface: Prevent a threat from being carried out.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means mostly or on the whole.

clue.text: Kings of Cologne who had many a soldier

parts.note: M, a thousand in Roman numerals
GI, an American soldier

explanation.surface: Monarchs of a German city commanded many troops.
explanation.walkthrough: The relics of the Three Kings are said to lie in Cologne Cathedral, so they are called the Kings of Cologne.
explanation.definitionFit: The wise men who visited the infant Jesus are traditionally the Three Kings.

clue.text: Characters in a rut must make a bloomer

indicators.note: characters means the letters of the phrase are used as a pool to rearrange

explanation.surface: People stuck in their ways will blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomer' looks like a blunder; it is something that blooms, a flower.
explanation.definitionFit: A nasturtium is a garden plant with bright orange flowers.

clue.text: Hire or fire -at the enemy

explanation.surface: Take on staff, or open fire on the foe.
explanation.definitionFit: To engage staff is to employ them, and to engage the enemy is to begin fighting it.

clue.text: Mad to call back after free exchange of quarters

indicators.note: after puts the reversed piece behind the first
quarters are compass points, so one point letter is swapped for another

parts.note: taken as written before the swap

indicators.note: back means the word for call is read in reverse

parts.note: to cite is to call or summon, as before a court

explanation.surface: Crazy to ring again after a free swap of rooms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exchange of quarters' swaps E (east) for N (north), making FREN; CITE read 'back' is ETIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Frenetic means frenzied, wildly agitated.
